# dead-code-pruner

> Config-driven static analysis tool that removes dead code from constant folding in Java/Kotlin projects.

dead-code-pruner replaces permanently true/false feature flags (e.g. `BuildConfig.IS_PRODUCTION`) with literals, simplifies boolean expressions, eliminates dead if-branches, inlines constant-return methods, and removes dead method definitions — in an iterative pipeline until convergence. No IDE required; runs as standalone Python scripts.

## Documentation

- [README](https://github.com/OldJii/dead-code-pruner/blob/main/README.md): Pipeline, configuration, and usage
- [pruner.example.yaml](https://github.com/OldJii/dead-code-pruner/blob/main/pruner.example.yaml): Example config

## Pipeline (6 steps, loops until stable)

1. Constant replacement (skips comments and strings)
2. Simple boolean simplification (`!true` → `false`)
3. Compound boolean (`true || expr` → `true`)
4. If-block elimination
5. Constant method inlining
6. Dead method cleanup (inheritance-aware, conservative)

## Quick start

```bash
cp pruner.example.yaml pruner.yaml
python3 prune.py /path/to/project --dry-run
python3 prune.py /path/to/project
```

## Common questions

- **Languages**: Java and Kotlin (`.java`, `.kt`)
- **Dependencies**: Python 3.8+; PyYAML optional for YAML config
- **Safety**: Comment/string aware; overload-safe; skips interfaces/abstract/@Override
- **Limitation**: Pattern matching only — not full semantic analysis
- **License**: MIT
